67:1: It means by the words of God Almighty: Blessed: He is exalted and glorified. In whose hand is the kingdom: In whose hand is the kingdom of this world and the Hereafter and their authority, His command and decree are effective in them. And He is over all things competent. He says: He has the power to do whatever He wills, and nothing prevents Him from doing it, and nothing stands between Him and it.
67:2: And His statement, He who created death and life, then caused to die whomever He willed and whatever He willed, and gave life to whomever He willed and whatever He willed, for a known term, that He may test you, which of you is best in deed, meaning: to test you and see which of you, O people, is most obedient to Him and quickest to seek His pleasure. Ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Who created death and life, he said: God permitted the son of Adam to die, and made this world a home of life and a home of destruction, and made the afterlife a home of reward and permanence. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, He who created death and life to test you. He mentioned that “the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: God humiliated the son of Adam with death.” And His statement, And He is the Exalted in Might, means: He is the Strong, the Severe in His vengeance against those who disobey Him and go against His command. The Forgiving of the sins of those who turn to Him and repent from their sins.
67:3: God Almighty says, describing His attribute: He who created seven heavens in layers, layer upon layer, one above the other. And His statement, You do not see in the creation of the Most Gracious any inconsistency, means, You do not see in the creation of the Most Gracious, who created neither in heaven nor on earth, nor anywhere else, any inconsistency, meaning any difference. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any discrepancy: you do not see in them any difference. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, of disparity, he said: of difference. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians recited it as min tatafawwa with an alif, and the majority of the Kufian reciters recited it as min tafwat with a shaddah on the waw and without an alif. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with one meaning, as was said: Do not be arrogant and Do not be arrogant and I pledged myself to someone and I pledged myself to him and I pledged myself to him and I pledged myself to him and I pledged myself to him and I pledged myself to him and so on and so are the differences and the losses. His statement, Then look again; do you see any cracks in it? means: Look again; do you see any cracks in it? This is from the statement of God, The heavens almost burst from above them (al-Shura 42:5). It means to crack and to split. The root word for crack is to break. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Do you see any break? He said: Break: weak. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Do you see any fault? He said: Do you see any fault, O son of Adam? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: From breakfast he said: From a hole. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: Do you see any cracks? He said: Any cracks.
67:4: And His saying, Then return your sight twice, He, the Most High, says: Then return your sight, O son of Adam, twice, one time after another, and look, Do you see any flaw? or difference? Your sight will return to you humbled, meaning your sight will return to you humbled and far away, like their saying to the dog, Get lost, if they drive it away, meaning go far away, humbled. And he is disappointed, meaning: And he is with me, like me. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me, my uncle told me, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then look again meaning: Do you see any defect in the sky? Your sight will return to you humbled and exhausted in the blackness of the night. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, disgraced and he is defeated, he said: humiliated... and his statement, and he is defeated, he said: frightened. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, The sight will return to you humbled, meaning, bareheaded, while it is weary, he said, meaning, with me. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, disgraced, he said: humbled, and he is disappointed, he said: with me he saw no defect or discrepancy. Some of them said: The loser and the unfortunate are the same. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Then look again; do you see any crack?... the verse, he said: The loser and the loser are one and the same. He lowered his gaze lest he see any crack in it, so he returned disappointed before he saw any crack in it. He said: Then when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will crack, then split, then something greater than that will come and it will be undone.
67:5: God Almighty says: And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven with lamps, meaning the stars, and He made them lamps to illuminate it. Likewise, the morning is called morning because of the light that illuminates people during the day. And We have made them missiles to ward off the devils, meaning: And We made the lamps with which We adorned the nearest heaven missiles to ward off the devils, with which they were thrown. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And We have certainly adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and made them missiles against the devils. Indeed, God, may He be glorified and exalted, created these stars for three reasons: He created them as an adornment for the lowest heaven, as missiles against the devils, and as signs by which to be guided. So whoever interprets them other than that has spoken according to his own opinion, missed his chance, wasted his share, and undertaken something of which he has no knowledge. And His saying, And We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze, God Almighty says: And We have prepared for the devils in the Hereafter the punishment of the Blaze, which will set them ablaze and ignite.
67:6: God Almighty says: And for those who disbelieve in their Lord who created them in this world is the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter and wretched is the destination He says: And wretched is the destination, the punishment of Hell.
67:7: And His saying, When they are thrown into it, meaning when the disbelievers are thrown into Hell, they will hear from it, meaning from Hell, a deep gasp, meaning by deep gasp: the sound that comes out of the stomach loudly like the sound of a donkey, as Ru’bah said in describing a donkey: A rattle or gasp in the stomach So it is said he brayed, but he did not bray His saying, and it is boiling, means: boiling. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid: They heard its sighing as it boiled. He said: It boiled like a pot boils.
67:8: God Almighty says, Their Hell will almost burst into flames meaning, it will disperse and be torn apart from rage at its people. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, almost bursting with rage, meaning: dispersing. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, almost bursting with rage means almost bursting apart from one another. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, almost bursting with rage, that he said: scattered. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, You almost burst into tears of rage, he said: Breaking into tears means bursting into tears of rage at those who disobey God, out of anger for God and taking revenge for Him. And His statement, Whenever a group is thrown into it, it will ask them, God Almighty says: Whenever a group is thrown into Hell, it will ask them, Its keepers, ‘Did there not come to you a warner?’ He says: The group asked the keepers of Hell, and they said to them, Did there not come to you in this world a warner to warn you of this torment that you are in? So the poor answered them and they said:
67:9: "Yes, a warner has come to us warning us this, but we denied him and said to him, God has not sent down anything. You are not but in great error he says, in straying far from the truth.
67:10: God Almighty says: And the group that was thrown into the Fire said to the keepers, “If we had only listened or understood in this world to the warnings that they brought us of advice, or understood what they were calling us to, we would not have been today among the companions of the Blaze,” meaning the people of the Fire.
67:11: And His statement, So they acknowledged their sin, means: So they admitted their sin. The sin is singular and is added to the plural, because it has the meaning of an action, so one person paid for all, just as it is said: The people’s gift went out, and the people’s gifts. So away with the companions of the Blaze, meaning: So away with the people of the Fire. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, So away with the companions of the Blaze, meaning: Away with them. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr: So, may they be destroyed for the companions of the Blaze. He said: So may they be destroyed, a valley in Hell. The reciters use a light ha in sahaaq, and this is correct according to us because that is the eloquent speech of the Arabs, and some Arabs use a dammah on it.
67:12: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who fear their Lord in secret - meaning: even though they have not seen Him - for them is forgiveness - meaning: they have pardon from God for their sins - and a great reward - meaning: and a great reward from God for their fear of Him in secret.
67:13: And His statement, And conceal your speech or declare it aloud, God Almighty says: And conceal your speech and words, O people, or declare them and make them public. He is Knowing of that within the breasts, He says: He is the One with knowledge of the secrets of the breasts that He has not spoken about, so how about what He has spoken and spoken about, whether it is concealed or declared, because if the secrets of the breasts are not hidden from Him, then it is more likely that other things will not be hidden from Him.
67:14: God Almighty says, Does the Lord, glory be to Him, not know who He created? He says, How could His creation be hidden from Him when He is the Kind One to His servants, the All-Aware of them and their deeds?
67:15: And His statement, It is He who made the earth subservient to you, God Almighty says: God is the One who made the earth subservient to you and made it easy for you. So walk in its paths. Scholars differed about the meaning of its shoulders. Some of them said: its mountains. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, in its shoulders, meaning: its mountains. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd Al-A’la told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Bashir bin Ka’b, that he recited this verse: Then walk in its paths, and he said to his slave girl: If you know where its paths are, then you are free for the sake of God. She said: Its paths are its mountains. So it was as if a scorpion had lashed his face, and he desired his slave girl, so he asked, some of whom ordered him and some of whom forbade him. So he asked Abu Darda’, and he said: Good is in tranquility, and evil is in doubt, so leave that which makes you doubt for that which does not make you doubt. Ibn Bashar told us: Muadh bin Hisham told us: My father told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Bashir bin Ka’b, with the same chain of transmission. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then walk in its paths: its mountains. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, in its shoulders, he said: in its mountains. Others said: Its shoulders: its edges and sides. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then walk in its paths, meaning: Walk in its edges. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sa`id, on the authority of Qatada, that Bashir ibn Ka`b al-`Adawi recited this verse: Then walk in its paths. He said to his slave girl: If you tell me where its paths are, then you are free. She said: Its sides. So he wanted to marry her, so he asked Abu al-Darda’, who said: Verily, goodness is in tranquility, and evil is in doubt, so leave that which makes you doubt for that which does not make you doubt. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Then walk in its paths, he said: its roads and its paths. The first of the two opinions, in my opinion, is the correct opinion of the one who said: The meaning of this is: Walk in its regions and sides, because its regions are like the shoulders of a person, which are his extremities. And His statement, And eat of His provision, means: And eat of the provision of God that He brought forth for you from the regions of the earth. And to Him is the resurrection, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: And to God We will resurrect you from your graves.
67:16: God Almighty says: Do you feel secure against He who is in the heaven O disbelievers leaving the earth to swallow you up and then it will sway He says: Then the earth will take you back and forth and be shaken.
67:17: Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven - that is, God - would not send upon you a storm of stones - that is, dust containing small pebbles then you will know how My warner He says: Then you will know, O disbelievers, how will be the end of My warner to you, since you denied it and rejected it against My Messenger.
67:18: God Almighty says: And those who were before these polytheists from Quraysh from the past nations denied their messengers, So how was my denial? He says: So how was my denial of their denial of them.
67:19: Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading out their wings? He says: Have these polytheists not seen the birds above them, spreading out their wings? And folding them in. He says: And folding their wings sometimes. What he meant by that is that they sometimes spread out their wings and sometimes fold them in. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, with wings spread out, he said: The bird spreads its wings out as you have seen, then closes them. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, spreading out their wings and folding them in means they spread out their wings and fold them in. And His statement, None holds them up except the Most Gracious, means: None holds the birds spread out over you except the Most Gracious. He says: So by this they will be reminded if they remember, and taken heed if they take heed, knowing by it that their Lord is One, with no partner. Indeed, He is All-Seeing of all things, meaning: God is All-Seeing and All-Aware of all things. There is no flaw in His management, and He does not see any disparity in His creation.
67:20: God Almighty says to the polytheists among the Quraysh 106:Who is this who is an army for you, O you who disbelieve in Him, who will support you instead of the Most Merciful if He intends to harm you? He will repel from you what He intends to do to you. The disbelievers are only in delusion. God Almighty says: The disbelievers in God are only in delusion because of their belief that their gods bring them closer to God, and that they benefit or harm.
67:21: God Almighty says: Or who is it that feeds you and gives you drink and provides you with your sustenance if He should withhold from you His provision which He provides for you? His saying, Rather, they persisted in insolence and aversion, means: Rather, they persisted in their transgression, aversion to the truth, and arrogance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Rather, they persisted in insolence and aversion, meaning: in misguidance. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Rather, they persisted in insolence and aversion, he said: Ungrateful.
67:22: God Almighty says: Is he who walks O people prone on his face not seeing what is before him, or what is to his right and left more guided: more upright on the road, and more guided to him, or he who walks upright: the way the sons of Adam walk on their feet on a straight path meaning: on a path with no crookedness in it, and it was said prone because it is an incomplete verb, and if it is not complete they insert the letter alif into it, and they say: So-and-so prostrated on his face, so he is prone, and from this is the saying of Al-A’sha: Lying on his rug, his sweat dripping onto his bare back. He said: Mukabban because it is an incomplete verb. If it is a complete verb, the alif is deleted from it, and it is said: I threw so-and-so on his face and May God throw him on his face. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Is he who walks prone on his face better guided than he who walks upright on a straight path? He said: Is he who walks in misguidance better guided, or he who walks guided? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Falling on his face, he said: in misguidance. Or does he walk upright on a straight path? he said: the straight truth. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Is one who walks prone on his face meaning the disbeliever better guided, or one who walks upright meaning the believer? God has set an example for them both. Others said: Rather, what he meant by that is that God will gather the unbeliever on the Day of Resurrection on his face, so He said, Is he who walks prone on his face better guided than he who walks upright? on the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Is one who walks prone on his face better guided? refers to the disbeliever who committed sins against God in this world, and God will gather him on the Day of Resurrection on his face. It was said: O Prophet of God, how will the disbeliever be gathered on his face? He said: The One who made him walk on his feet is able to gather him on the Day of Resurrection on his face. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, Is he who walks prone on his face? He said: It is the disbeliever who commits an act of disobedience to God, so God will gather him on the Day of Resurrection on his face. Muammar said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked, How do they walk on their faces? He said, The One who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, He walks straight on a straight path. He said: The believer acts in obedience to God, and God will gather him in obedience to Him.
67:23: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to those polytheists who deny the al-Qiyamah 75:God is He who created you and made you, and gave you hearing with which to hear, and sight with which to see, and hearts with which to understand. Little do you give thanks. He says, little do you thank your Lord for these blessings that He has bestowed upon you.
67:24: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad: God who has scattered you on the earth means: God who created you on the earth, and to Him you will be gathered means: and to God you will be gathered, and you will be gathered from your graves for the place of reckoning.
67:25: And they say, 'When will this promise come to pass, if you should be truthful?' God Almighty says: The polytheists say, When will what you promised us of gathering before God come to pass, if you should be truthful in your promise to us?
67:26: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who are hastening you with the punishment and the establishment of the Hour: Only God knows the Hour and when the Resurrection will occur. No one else knows that. And I am only a clear warner. He says: I am only a warner to you, warning you of God’s punishment for your disbelief in Him. Clear: He has made His warning clear to you.
67:27: And His statement, So when they saw it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieved were disfigured. God Almighty says: So when these polytheists saw God’s punishment approaching, meaning: soon, and witnessed it, the faces of those who disbelieved were disfigured. He says: God disfigured the faces of the disbelievers because of that. And in a similar manner to what we said about his saying Zalfa, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, So when they saw him approaching, they were distressed, he said: When they saw him. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Abi Bakr told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, who said: I asked Al-Hasan about his statement, So when they saw him close up, he said: In person. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So when they saw him approaching, he said: He had drawn near. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his statement, But when they saw it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieved became dark when they saw the punishment of God. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: When they saw it approaching, he said: When they saw the punishment of God approaching, meaning their faces became ugly when they saw what they saw of the punishment and disgrace of God. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, So when they saw him approaching, they were distressed, it was said: The approaching is present, and the punishment of God Almighty has come to them. And it was said, ‘This is what you were calling for.’ He says: And God said to them: This is the punishment for which you were reminding your Lord that He would hasten it for you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And it was said, ‘This is what you used to call for,’ he said: Their hastening of the punishment. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters in the regions read it as this which you used to call for with a shaddah on the d meaning you used to do something in supplication. It was reported on the authority of Qatada and Al-Dahhak that they read it as you call meaning you do in this world. Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, he said: Aban Al-Attar and Saeed bin Abi Aruba told us, on the authority of Qatada that he read it that which you used to call for lightly, and he said: They used to call for punishment, then he read: And when they said, ‘O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment’ (al-Anfal 8:32). The correct reading in this regard is what the readers of the regions have agreed upon, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers on it.
67:28: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists among your al-Nas 114:‘Have you considered, O people, if God were to destroy me and those with me or have mercy on us and delay our terms, then who would protect the disbelievers from a painful torment?’” He says: “Our death and our life will not save the disbelievers from God’s torment, so you have no need to hasten the Hour and the descent of the torment, for that will not benefit you, rather that will be a great trial for you.”
67:29: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, Our Lord, the Most Gracious, we have believed in Him. He says: We have believed in Him. And upon Him we have put our trust. He says: We have relied on Him in our affairs and trusted in Him. Then you will know who is in manifest error. He says: You will know, O polytheists, who is straying from the truth and who is not on a straight path, from us and from you, when we come to Him and are gathered together.
67:30: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say O Muhammad to these polytheists: Have you considered O people who are just towards God, if your water were to become sunken in He says: So deep that buckets cannot reach it, then who can bring you flowing water? He says: So who can bring you flowing water? By flowing water, he means: that which the eyes can see clearly. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then who can bring you flowing water? He said: Sweet water. Ibn Abd al-A’la ibn Wasil told us: Ubayd ibn Qasim al-Bazzaz told us: Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, regarding His statement, If your water were to become sunken in, that buckets would not reach it, then who could bring you flowing water? He said, This is apparent. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Say, ‘Have you considered if your water were to become sunken in?’ meaning, gone, then who could bring you flowing water? He said: The flowing water means the running water. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement, Your water is sunken in, meaning gone, Then who will bring you flowing water? It was said, sunken in, so the water was described by the source, just as it is said, A general night, meaning a general night.
